_meta.scope: Australia (AU) and New Zealand (NZ) tiling data for an iPhone tiling calculator

conventions.derived: true means the value was calculated by the researcher from the cited figures (for example pieces x tile area, or bag kg / m2), not printed by the source
conventions.UNVERIFIED: the value could not be confirmed from a primary or retailer page during this research
conventions.verifiedVia: how the value was read: 'page' = product or manufacturer page read directly, 'tds' = manufacturer data sheet PDF text read directly, 'secondary' = industry body or third-party copy, 'searchSnippet' = search-result text only (page itself could not be opened)

grout.formula: kg/m2 = ((A + B) / (A x B)) x C x D x 1.6, where A = tile length mm, B = tile width mm, C = tile thickness mm, D = joint width mm
grout.formulaNote: A-D definitions are printed in the AU TDS; the 1.6 constant is printed as an image and was confirmed from a Mapei catalogue copy (archiexpo). It matches the AU TDS table (e.g. 300x300x10 @ 3 mm = 0.3 kg/m2).

standards.name: AS 3958:2023 Installation of ceramic and stone tiles
standards.note: Combines and replaces AS 3958.1-2007 (and AS 3958.2). Store lists AS 3958.1-2007 as superseded. Many manufacturer TDS still cite AS 3958.1 (e.g. Davco Ultraflex movement joints at max 4.5 m centres).

standards.name: AS 3958.1-2007 Ceramic tiles - Guide to the installation of ceramic tiles (superseded)
standards.note: Superseded; keep only as a legacy reference.

standards.name: AS 3740:2021 Waterproofing of domestic wet areas
standards.note: Current edition, published 23 Jul 2021, replaced AS 3740-2010. Called up by NCC Housing Provisions 10.2.1(2). Detailed clause values are behind a paywall and were not read (UNVERIFIED beyond NCC text).

standards.name: NCC 2022 Housing Provisions Part 10.2 Wet area waterproofing
standards.note: Shower walls waterproof >= 1800 mm above floor substrate (10.2.2(1)(b)); shower wall junctions >= 40 mm each side (10.2.2(1)(c)); unenclosed shower waterstop >= 1500 mm from shower rose (10.2.18); step-down >= 25 mm below floor outside (10.2.15); hob membrane over top, down outside, >= 50 mm onto floor (10.2.28); hobs not timber (10.2.16(4)); outside shower: wall/floor junctions waterproof, horizontal flashing leg >= 40 mm (10.2.3); perimeter flashing vertical leg >= 25 mm above FFL, horizontal leg >= 50 mm (10.2.24); walls by non-freestanding bath within 75 mm of wall water resistant >= 150 mm above vessel (10.2.4); sinks/vessels within 75 mm of wall: 150 mm (10.2.5).

standards.name: NCC 2022 Housing Provisions 10.2.12 Falls to floor wastes
standards.note: Where a floor waste is installed: continuous fall min 1:80, max 1:50.

standards.name: AS/NZS 4858:2004 Wet area membranes
standards.note: Membrane classes I-III by elongation; K10 Plus and WPM 155 Rapid Plus are Class III.

standards.name: AS 4654.2 Waterproofing membranes for external above-ground use - Design and installation
standards.note: Balconies, decks and other external above-ground membranes; edition year not verified (2012 commonly cited).

standards.name: AS 4586 (slip resistance classification), via NCC Housing Provisions Table 11.2.4
standards.note: Stair treads: dry P3 or R10, wet P4 or R11. Nosing or landing edge strip: dry P3, wet P4. Ramps not steeper than 1:8: dry P4 or R10, wet P5 or R12.

standards.name: AS 1428.1 Design for access and mobility (contrasting nosing strips, NCC Volume One)
standards.note: Secondary sources: contrasting strip 50-75 mm wide, max 15 mm setback from nosing, >= 30% luminance contrast, max 10 mm down the riser. Which edition (2009 or 2021) the NCC DTS references is disputed between sources; applies to Class 2-9 buildings, not houses. UNVERIFIED against primary text.

stairs.note: NCC 2022 Housing Provisions Table 11.2.2a (stairs other than spiral).

falls.shower: 1:80 min to 1:50 max to the floor waste (NCC 2022 HP 10.2.12 applies wherever a floor waste is installed)
falls.outside: Same 1:80-1:50 where the floor has a waste; a floor with a vessel must be graded to a floor waste (SA variation 10.2.33). Davco K10 Plus TDS advises 1:80 for wet areas and 1:100 for balconies/rooftops (manufacturer advice, not code).
falls.oldValues: 1:60-1:80 shower falls were from older editions (pre-2022); 1:60 is no longer the NCC limit.

standards.name: NZ Building Code clause E3 Internal moisture; Acceptable Solution E3/AS1 (2nd edition, Amendment 7, effective 5 Nov 2020)
standards.note: Per LEVEL (BRANZ): tiles max 6% water absorbency; shower floor and wall finishes impervious; enclosures continuous from floor/top of upstand to >= 1800 mm above floor and >= 300 mm above the rose; open showers fall >= 1:50 to the waste within 1500 mm radius of the point below the rose (E3/AS1 3.3.2.3); floor wastes to G13/AS1.

standards.name: E3/AS2 Internal wet-area membrane systems (1st edition)
standards.note: Cites the Waterproof Membrane Association Code of Practice for internal wet-area membrane systems (4th ed., Feb 2020); membranes must comply with AS/NZS 4858:2004; all components from one supplier; contained by a waterstop.

standards.name: AS/NZS 4858:2004 Wet area membranes
standards.note: Class I (least flexible) to Class III (most flexible, suits timber framing).

standards.name: NZBC clause B2 Durability
standards.note: Waterproofing systems under wet-area tiling need at least 15 years durability.

standards.name: NZBC clause D1 Access routes; Acceptable Solution D1/AS1 (2nd edition, Amendment 6) Table 6
standards.note: Primary PDF could not be text-extracted; values taken from BRANZ Bulletin 625 (2018) and BRANZ 'External stairs for houses'. Max 5 mm variation between steps; closed nosing projection 0-25 mm, open stair 15-25 mm.

standards.name: D1/AS1 section 2.1 Slip resistance (AS/NZS 3661.1; AS 4586-2013 as an alternative)
standards.note: Level public access routes: coefficient of friction >= 0.4 (D1/AS1 2.1.1); stairs and slopes need slightly higher (Table 2 notes); a house bathroom is unlikely to be an 'access route'. Secondary source says level routes may instead meet SRV >= 39 under AS 4586-2013 or Table 2 'acceptable wet slip' (UNVERIFIED against current D1/AS1 text).

standards.name: NZS 4121 Design for access and mobility
standards.note: UNVERIFIED - not researched; relevance to contrasting nosings in NZ not confirmed.

stairs.riserMin: UNVERIFIED (D1/AS1 sets a recommended minimum pitch of 23 deg rather than a minimum riser)
stairs.twoRplusGNote: NZ does not use a 2R+G band; BRANZ says the old 2R+G = 580-610 rule of thumb should not be used. Check pitch, riser and going instead.

falls.shower: Open (level-entry/unenclosed) showers: fall not less than 1:50 to the floor waste within a 1500 mm radius of the point below the shower rose (E3/AS1 3.3.2.3, via LEVEL/BRANZ). Falls must be formed in the substrate or screed, not by the membrane.
falls.enclosedShower: UNVERIFIED (no separate NZ code fall found for enclosed showers with an upstand)

upstand.term: upstand (NZ code wording; 'hob' is also used by BRANZ)

falls.term: falls / fall to the floor waste
